name: PopNow
tagline: A pay-per-run front end for hosted image, video and music models, with one-tap photo-to-video effect presets.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The software here is a router: pick a model, fill a template prompt, show the cost, run it, keep the output in a gallery. An agent can rebuild that in a session on top of fal.ai or Replicate, and the 160 effects are mostly prompt presets plus a reference image, which is a JSON file you can grow yourself. What you cannot rebuild is model access: the good video and music models are rented, not run, so your DIY version is a thinner skin over the same bill. Call it kinda because the app survives the clone but the dependency does not go away, and a handful of marquee models are only licensed to specific aggregators.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app that lists hosted models with their per-run price, applies a library of effect presets to an uploaded photo or prompt, submits the job, polls for the result and files it in a searchable gallery.
requirements: a fal.ai or Replicate API key with billing attached
somewhere to put output files, local disk is fine
patience for per-model input schemas, they are all slightly different
whatYouLose: Curated effect presets that someone already tuned against each model, instead of your own trial and error
Mobile apps, which is where one-tap photo-to-video actually gets used
Access to models that are exclusive to a given aggregator or not on any public API at all
A price estimate that matches the actual invoice, since you now eat raw provider pricing plus failed runs
Any queue management or retry logic beyond what you bother to write
moatNotes: The moat is plumbing to many model vendors plus the taste to wrap each one in a preset that reliably works. Neither is hard, both are tedious, and the tedium is the product.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because nobody wants to debug a video model's input schema at 11pm. Paying per run with the price shown up front removes the two things people hate about raw APIs: surprise bills and reading docs. The effect library is also real work, a preset that turns a selfie into a specific animated look is tuned, not guessed, and reproducing fifty of those yourself is a project, not an afternoon. If you only generate a few clips a month, the markup is cheaper than your evening.
notes: Clone the router, rent the same models, save the markup and lose the presets.
prompt:
Build a local, single-user AI media studio called "runbench" in an empty folder. No accounts, no cloud deploy, no telemetry.

Stack, no substitutions: Next.js 15 App Router with TypeScript, Tailwind, SQLite via better-sqlite3, and fal.ai as the only model provider (@fal-ai/client). Run with `npm run dev` on port 3000.

Secrets: FAL_KEY in .env.local, read server-side only. Commit a .env.example. Never send the key to the browser.

Data model in SQLite: models (id, slug, kind: image|video|audio, fal_endpoint, price_per_run_usd, input_schema_json), presets (id, model_id, name, prompt_template, needs_image, default_params_json), runs (id, model_id, preset_id, prompt, input_image_path, status, output_path, cost_usd, error, created_at).

Seed models.json and presets.json as checked-in files, not hardcoded in code. Seed with 6 models across image, video and audio using real fal endpoint slugs, and 12 presets whose prompt_template uses {{subject}} style placeholders. Make it obvious how to add more by editing JSON and rerunning `npm run seed`.

UI, three pages:
1. / : grid of presets with kind filter, each card shows the preset name, the model it runs on and "$X.XX per run" from the model price. Clicking opens a run drawer with a prompt box, optional image upload, and a confirm button labeled with the exact cost.
2. /runs : reverse-chronological list of every run with status, thumbnail or audio player, cost, and total spend this month summed from the runs table.
3. /models : editable table of price_per_run_usd so prices stay honest when fal changes them.

Server behavior: POST /api/run inserts a queued row, submits to fal with the preset's merged params, polls until done, downloads the output to ./output/{run_id}.{ext}, and updates the row. On failure store the error text and still keep the row. Serve outputs through a route handler, not the public folder.

In scope: upload to fal storage for image inputs, a running cost total, re-run a past run with one click.
Out of scope: auth, payments, multi-user, queues beyond in-process polling, mobile app, video editing, any provider other than fal.

README: how to get a FAL_KEY, how to add a model, and a clear line saying prices in models.json are user-maintained and may drift from fal's actual billing.
